etymologies.etymologyHTML: Shortening of Hamburger sandwich, Hamburger steak, etc.; or, less likely, borrowed from German Hamburger (“native of Hamburg”), equivalent to Hamburg +‎ -er. (Can this etymology be sourced?)

definitions.definition: A hot sandwich consisting of a patty of cooked ground beef or a meat substitute, in a sliced bun, usually also containing salad vegetables, condiments, or both.
The patty used in such a sandwich.
(uncountable) Ground beef, especially that intended to be made into hamburgers.
(US, colloquial, somewhat crude) An animal or human, or the flesh thereof, that has been badly injured as a result of an accident or conflict.
(graphical user interface) Short for hamburger button.
(US, education, informal) Describing the shape of a rectangular piece of paper folded in half so that it forms a short rectangle.

quote.text: Why they didn’t both break their necks or get hamburgered by cloven hooves was a mystery.
